Main effects (contrast ‘favourite drinks > neutral cues’) are displayed in Fig. 2 and in Table 1 .

The findings indicate higher cue-induced activation in light social drinkers than in heavy drinkers in regions associated with reward processing.

spans.text: Light social drinkers showed a higher BOLD response in the right globus pallidus [(x,y,z) = (20,–10,4), t = 3.65], P < 0.001 uncorrected (whole brain analysis) compared to heavy social drinkers.

name.value: light social drinkers compared to heavy social drinkers (ROI)

definition.value: Enhanced activation in the bilateral ventral striatum and the prefrontal cortex in light social drinkers compared to heavy social drinkers.

value: ROI analyses revealed an enhanced activation in the bilateral ventral striatum and the prefrontal cortex in light social drinkers compared to heavy social drinkers.

Increased prefrontal activation in light social drinkers may indicate that they activate cortical control when viewing alcohol cues, which may prevent the development of heavy drinking or alcohol dependence.

name.value: increased activation in heavy drinkers during the presentation of alcohol cues

definition.value: Increased activation of the left fusiform gyrus and the left dorsal striatum in heavy drinkers during the presentation of alcohol cues.

value: Whole-brain analyses showed increased activation of the left fusiform gyrus and the left dorsal striatum in heavy drinkers during the presentation of alcohol cues.
Heavy drinkers may not be able to acquire cortical control over behaviour when alcohol cues are presented.

name.value: heavy drinkers compared to light drinkers (ROI)

definition.value: Enhanced cue-induced activation in the bilateral dorsal striatum in heavy drinkers compared to light drinkers.

value: ROI analyses showed enhanced cue-induced activation in the bilateral dorsal striatum in heavy drinkers compared to light drinkers.

Higher alcohol cue-induced activation of the dorsal striatum in heavy drinkers compared to light social drinkers is in accordance with the hypothesis of a shift of learning processes from ventral to dorsal domains of the striatum when alcohol dependence proceeds.
